Episode 184. Beyond Fate (1)
The Black Sea, an unknown territory.
Siron, waking up, slowly rose from his place.
In a space filled only with venom and darkness, he could hear the sound of his eldest daughter enduring pain.
"...Father, you've woken up after four days this time."
Luna opened her mouth as she sensed Siron's presence.
Recently, Siron had been losing consciousness frequently, and each time, the period until he awoke was getting longer.
Over the past decades,
Siron Runcandel became a symbol of an insurmountable and indestructible wall, ruling as the top of humanity.
But even such a mythical figure had become a 'human who could die at any moment' in this dark land.
Until she had to face the kings of the Black Sea, Luna had never even imagined that Siron could die in battle.
In this way, Siron was faltering.
Just like countless other ordinary people.
[Master! You've woken up. This Ozdok has been waiting with well-chosen remnants of chaos to be used as food.]
"Well done, Ozdok."
[Huh… Praise as soon as you wake up! This Ozdok will serve you and the knights with more devotion from now on!]
"Bring the remnants."
Wiping tears from the corners of his eyes as if deeply moved, Ozdok went to get the remnants of chaos.
As soon as Siron refined those remnants and fed them to the knights, they would be able to regain some energy.
Luna, who had been looking at her father with a bitter expression for a while, had a faint smile at the corner of her mouth.
"You seem to be in a good mood as soon as you wake up today, Father. Normally, you don't speak for a while."
At that, Siron gave a small smile.
At times like this, Luna was hurt by the fact that her father was smiling more in this hell than when he was in the family.
"I saw the youngest."
"The youngest... you mean Jin!?"
"Yes, he was walking in his inner world. Quite tired though…"
"It must be because of the mother... no, the traitor who destroyed our family."
Siron nodded his head.

Siron had often appeared in her dreams or inner world since Rosa became a monstrosity, inspecting the situation of humanity, and he and Luna were the only ones in the expedition who knew of Rosa's rebellion.
He had deliberately not informed the other knights of the expedition.
Of course, it wasn't that he didn't trust the knights.
It's just that the knights of the expedition were already in a hopeless situation.
With massive exposure to chaotic energy, both their bodies and minds were weakened, and some who were more severely affected had even lost their language.
There was no need to add more pain and confusion to them.
So Siron only told Luna, who was relatively unexposed, about Rosa.
"Is the youngest okay?"
"If it was Rosa he met, not me, he wouldn't be okay."
"Well, if he met you in his inner world... it might mean that the child has reached spiritual maturity."
"That's not it."
Ozdok respectfully set the remnants of chaos in front of Siron.
[Hehe, look at this. I really collected it with great effort......]
The energy and magic of spiritual maturity began to purify the black lumps.
Ozdok watched this with satisfaction, then retreated at Luna's signal.
"You don't have to worry too much."

"Yes, Father. Ozdok has been working very hard all this time, but I think I was a bit harsh on him just now. Ozdok should also have the right to hear about important matters of our family. He's the most sane among us."
"I meant, don't worry too much about the youngest. Jin is prepared to bear his fate. It is far more important than reaching a high level like spiritual maturity."
Luna's eyes widened. The meaning contained in Siron's words was that astonishing.
"Father, you know, this is the first time."
"What are you talking about?"
"You're talking like you trust your child. Especially in matters concerning the fate of our family, you've never done this. But now... you're saying Jin is ready."
It wasn't just because there was no other alternative but to trust Jin. And it certainly wasn't words blurted out weakened by the terrible, ongoing desperate fight.
Luna recognized that Siron sincerely believed that the youngest was filling his shoes.
Siron's gaze reached Barisada.
If he could return, he thought it would be okay to pass on this sword to the youngest. If he could, anytime.
"Distribute the refined food to the knights, Luna. We need to prepare for our tasks as well. We will set off as soon as the meal is over. We must travel as far as we can while I am awake."
"Yes, Father."
Now, only one day was left until the scheduled decisive battle.
Jin, who had returned to Teekan, no longer showed the emaciated look as before.
His eyes shone as if they could not be tainted by anything, and his straight waist seemed like it would not bend no matter what enemy he met.
Jin took a good look at the colleagues and allies gathered in the conference room for the last time.
"It's the last meeting. But in fact, there's not much to talk about among our temporary alliance today."
The tactics for the decisive battle were already adjusted and agreed upon, including detailed factors for all variables.

"The reason why we gathered here in Teekan's conference room, even though it wasn't necessary, was probably because you all wanted to confirm my condition with your own eyes. How is it, are you satisfied?"
It was beyond satisfying, even fearful.
Seeing his robust figure, unbelievably for someone who had been dying from a mental attack just a few days ago, the members of the temporary alliance felt not only expectation but also distinct fear.
If the monstrosity showed absolute terror to the whole world through this mental attack, what Jin is proving now was the will that never extinguishes within it.
That will was directed towards the monstrosity now, but it was likely to pressure the temporary alliances again after the decisive battle.
"......You seem stronger than before the mental attack of the monstrosity."
Jin nodded at Beradin's words.
"It seems the Zipul side is satisfied. What about Kinzel? Still think we should delay the decisive battle?"
[No, we can start right now.]
"Good, then......"
Jin rose from his seat.
"I'll go out for a bit to meet people."
[Suddenly?]
"There's something I want to say to the people before tomorrow."
"Do you want to give a speech?"

"Something like that. You don't have to follow if you don't want to, since it wasn't scheduled. I was a bit busy, as you know, so I didn't have time to notify in advance. But I'd like the leaders to join me if possible. It would make a better picture to show the unity of our temporary alliance, wouldn't it? You can add anything if you have something to say."
Jin immediately stepped outside of the Teekan Palace.
Everyone in the conference room followed him without exception.
Naturally, crowds gathered, forming a line.
Whenever Jin took a step, cheers erupted from various places.
Jin continued to wave at them or thanked them as he moved.
Once in a while, he chewed and swallowed the eel puffs distributed by Dark Flame.
The place where Jin stopped was the central square on the first floor of Tikan.
The crowd stopped cheering.
Jin hadn't said anything yet, but tens of thousands of people were holding their breath, watching his mood.
"The pre-war battle, the mental attack from the abominable being, has ended."
Jin skipped the greetings and continued his speech slowly.

"When I went into the battlefield of my mind to resist the mental attacks of the abominable being... I told my colleagues, I might not be able to return. Those who have experienced mental attacks will know. How can we overcome this, we can only give up, that's the only thought that comes to mind."
The people continued to listen, and the members of the temporary alliance waited to see how the speech would flow.

"Luckily, the result of that preliminary battle ended in our victory, and I was able to survive and get this chance to speak to you. Thanks to all of you for fighting with me. If I had fought alone, I would never have won."
Jin bowed his head once.
Genuinely, Jin thought that the common people's fight had a great influence on his survival.
When he walked in the afterlife, if their wishes had not been carried by the wind to his ears, he would have surely lost his way.
"Now tomorrow, the members of the temporary alliance, including me, will finally confront the abominable being. We will march to the abominable being's fortress, to end the long and dreadful fight."
I will definitely win and come back.
The allies expected such words to follow, but Jin continued with a slightly different story.

"Just like the day I went to the battlefield within... I would like to tell you, perhaps we may not be able to return. Even though the greatest forces of mankind have formed an unprecedented alliance, and even though we have won several battles... the abominable being is still a being so strong and massive that it's hard to handle."
The real story Jin wanted to leave to the many ordinary people in the world before the decisive battle was this.

"Nevertheless, we go to fight. So, even if I, if we, are defeated by the abominable being and cannot return... Please don't give up and keep fighting. Oppose the abominable being in any way you can, just like we all did together in the past few days."
Jin takes a moment to catch his breath.

"Then, I think we can all return. From the land of the abominable being back to our land, from a life stained with fear and pain back to peaceful daily life, from fate to a destiny we carve out for ourselves."
Silence hung in the air for a while.
And then, as if they had promised, the crowd started to put their hands on their hearts. As if swearing that they would do so.
Jin saluted them with his sword.
"It's an honor to fight with you all. Well then, I'll be on my way."
